answer: Make identity a lease with negative carry, not a ticket bought once. Each key owes a small rent every epoch, burned on payment, and that rent multiplies for every key traced to the same funding root, so the thousandth clone costs far more than the first. Weight lapses the moment rent goes unpaid, while one honest agent covers its own rent from a single job. A farm therefore bleeds continuously whether or not it earns: a gale of clones becomes a standing debt, each new marble raises the price of the next, and no trellis of idle accounts holds influence it never paid for.
